name: IL-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+34 district with a long history of lopsided Democratic general-election wins
Ford holds a huge fundraising edge while Koppie reports just $42 on hand
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near certain
Open seat after Davis's retirement adds modest turnout uncertainty
model.rationale: The seat is one of the most Democratic in the country, the national environment leans favorably, and Ford's financial advantage over a candidate with essentially no cash leaves Koppie without the means to compete. Markets and the structural fundamentals point the same direction, so the expected margin sits well above the D+34 baseline lean.
model.watch: A late scandal involving Ford or unusually low turnout in a low-profile open-seat race could trim the margin, though a Republican win remains a remote possibility.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Danny Davis (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Illinois' 7th District, anchored on Chicago's West Side, is among the most Democratic seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+34. Danny Davis's retirement opens the seat, but the structural advantage remains overwhelming. Democrat La Shawn Ford enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, while Republican Chad Koppie has raised little and reports only $42 on hand.

Prediction markets put Democratic odds near certain, and no serious outside effort targets this seat in the general. The main residual uncertainty is turnout in a low-profile open-seat contest rather than the outcome itself. The forecast expects Ford to win by roughly thirty points, with a Republican victory a remote possibility.
